subsystems.name: Neural sensor
subsystems.role: records the brain or nerve signals that will drive the limb.
parts: penetrating microelectrode arrays (on the order of 100 stiff silicon shanks)

subsystems.name: Implant electronics
subsystems.role: amplifies, digitises and transmits neural activity from inside the body.
parts: inductive or wireless power and data link

subsystems.name: Decoder
subsystems.role: turns firing patterns into movement commands in real time.
parts: machine-learning model (e.g. Kalman filter or neural network)

subsystems.name: Prosthetic limb
subsystems.role: the actuated hand, wrist, elbow or whole arm.

subsystems.name: Sensory feedback channel
subsystems.role: returns touch and limb position to the user so control feels natural.
parts: stimulating electrodes on nerve or cortex

subsystems.name: Attachment and interface
subsystems.role: connects the device to the body mechanically and keeps the tissue healthy.
parts: targeted muscle reinnervation (rerouting severed nerves to spare muscle)

buildSteps.title: Choose the signal source
buildSteps.detail: Designers pick cortical electrodes for paralysis or high dexterity, or nerve and muscle signals for a residual limb, trading invasiveness against signal quality.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Silicon shanks are micromachined and coated with conductive and insulating layers, or polymer films are patterned with metal tracks and contact sites.

buildSteps.title: Package and seal the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Circuitry is sealed in a hermetic case with feedthroughs, because body fluid destroys unprotected electronics within months.

buildSteps.title: Implant surgically
buildSteps.detail: A craniotomy exposes the cortex for array insertion, or a cuff is wrapped around a nerve; the device is anchored and the wound closed.

buildSteps.title: Record and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: The user watches or attempts movements while the system records, so the decoder learns the mapping from neural activity to intended motion.

buildSteps.title: Close the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Decoder output drives the limb's motors, and the control is tuned over sessions as the user adapts and the decoder is retrained.

buildSteps.title: Add sensory feedback
buildSteps.detail: Stimulation is delivered to nerve or cortex in step with the hand's sensors, and the intensity is tuned until the user reports predictable sensations.

buildSteps.title: Fit the mechanical interface
buildSteps.detail: A socket or osseointegrated implant is made so loads pass into the skeleton rather than pinching soft tissue.

buildSteps.title: Maintain and recalibrate
buildSteps.detail: Signal quality drifts as tissue reacts to the implant, so the decoder is periodically retrained and the hardware monitored.

prerequisites.why: signals from implanted arrays fade over months to years as scar tissue forms, which is the main limit on multi-year use.

prerequisites.tech: Hermetic implantable electronics and wireless power
prerequisites.why: cochlear implants and deep brain stimulators have used sealed cases and inductive links for decades.
decoders in laboratory trials have let paralysed participants move robotic arms within a fraction of a second of intent.
nerve and cortical stimulation can produce touch, but the sensations are coarse and hard to place precisely.
commercial powered hands and elbows are already widely fitted; a BCI mainly changes how they are commanded.

pathway.milestone: commercial myoelectric hands with pattern-recognition control, plus surgical nerve rerouting for better signals
pathway.unlocks: useful daily-life function for many people with limb loss, without brain implants.

pathway.milestone: implanted cortical interfaces in small clinical trials (e.g. the BrainGate line of research) giving paralysed participants dexterous control of a robotic or virtual arm
pathway.unlocks: proof that brain-driven control works outside the laboratory setting.

pathway.milestone: fully implanted, wireless systems with sensory feedback used at home for months
pathway.unlocks: everyday independence without a cable through the skin or a technician present.

pathway.milestone: electrodes that survive a decade and are implanted with less invasive surgery
pathway.unlocks: routine clinical use rather than research participation, and eventual use for paralysis and nerve injury as well as amputation.
